title: ci_starvation.py ignored --repo on the gh route, so private-monorepo CI could not be classified
problem: Runs on bet work merge private-monorepo PRs whose CI dies in 2-16 s. With gh on PATH (cloud sessions have it), ci_starvation.py sent `repos/{owner}/{repo}/...` to gh, which resolves the placeholder from the local remote, so `--repo Duncan-Haywood/private-monorepo` was silently ignored and the tool read this repository. Runs classified private runs by hand from actions_get runner_id.
evidence: 2026-11-25 `promptctl.py measure`, Doc friction by file: 'private-monorepo CI' 5 live reports, verify-and-merge.md 2 of 3 live reports and prompt.md 1 say ci_starvation.py only reads this repo

2026-11-25: `ci_starvation.py --repo Duncan-Haywood/private-monorepo --run 1` before the fix asked gh for repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/1/jobs (this repo); after, it asks repos/Duncan-Haywood/private-monorepo/...
change: fetch() substitutes an explicit --repo on every route; verify-and-merge.md 'Reading CI' names --repo for the private repository and --from-json with saved MCP jobs JSON when gh cannot read it.
metric: doc_friction entries in 7 days after merge saying private CI could not be classified with ci_starvation.py
source: process run 2026-11-25 (critique: live doc_friction clusters from promptctl measure)

history.note: Shipped; verify after a week of runs.
